name: nuclei-autotriage
description: Two-stage LLM triage pipeline (falsifier + red-team pass) for Nuclei JSONL findings via OpenAI-compatible endpoints (vLLM/Ollama). Deduplicates and prioritizes scanner output.
use_case: Post-scan triage of Nuclei findings. Feed raw JSONL output, get ranked prioritized results with false-positive filtering.
kerrigan_relevance: CrashTriageEngine analog — same two-pass (classify → verify) pattern Kerrigan uses for crash deduplication.

name: honeyslop
description: Code-canary decoys to detect and triage AI-hallucinated vulnerability reports flooding bug-bounty programs. Identifies slop submissions automatically.
use_case: Bug bounty programs receiving LLM-generated false reports. Deploy canaries, auto-reject AI-hallucinated findings.
kerrigan_relevance: Defensive complement to Kerrigan's harness generation — canaries catch hallucinated vulns before they waste researcher time.

name: nano-analyzer
description: Minimal three-stage LLM pipeline (context → scan → skeptical triage) for zero-day discovery in C/C++ codebases.
use_case: C/C++ zero-day discovery with LLM-driven code analysis. Three-stage: gather context, scan for patterns, skeptically verify.
kerrigan_relevance: Same target domain as Kerrigan's harness generation — complementary static analysis before dynamic fuzzing.

name: ai-soc-triage-assistant
description: SOC alert triage assistant with prompt-injection guardrails, output validation, and MITRE ATT&CK mapping. Handles high-volume alert queues.
use_case: SOC teams with alert fatigue. Routes, deduplicates, and MITRE-maps incoming alerts automatically.
kerrigan_relevance: CyberGuard integration point — alert triage logic maps directly to CyberGuard's incident report generator.

name: agent-audit
description: Forensic auditor for local AI coding agents (Claude Code, Codex CLI, OpenClaw) and project-surface scanner for repos shipping skills, plugins, and MCP manifests. 296 bundled rules across native and imported detector families, with optional LLM cross-verification.
use_case: Auditing AI agent deployments for supply-chain risk. Scans CLAUDE.md, skills/, .mcp configs, and agent logs.
kerrigan_relevance: Direct application to Kerrigan's own skill surface — run agent-audit against Kerrigan's skills/ and loop/ directories.

name: aguara
description: Single-binary static scanner (Go, no LLM) for AI-agent skills and MCP servers. Multi-layer engine: pattern matching, NLP, taint tracking, and rug-pull detection. Companion aguara-mcp exposes scanning as an MCP tool.
use_case: Zero-dependency scan of MCP server manifests and agent skill definitions. CI/CD pipeline integration.
kerrigan_relevance: No-LLM fallback scanner — runs before Kerrigan's own verification pass on generated harnesses.

name: agent-scan
description: Security scanner for AI agents, MCP servers, and agent skills by Snyk. Successor to Invariant Labs mcp-scan. Integrates with Snyk platform for vulnerability tracking.
use_case: Enterprise AI agent security scanning with CVE tracking and fix suggestions.
kerrigan_relevance: Enterprise-grade complement to agent-audit — use in CyberGuard's compliance reporting pipeline.

name: skill-scanner
description: Scanner for agent skills combining YAML + YARA patterns, LLM-as-a-judge, and behavioral dataflow analysis. Covers Codex and Cursor skill formats.
use_case: Scanning AI coding agent skill definitions for malicious patterns, data exfiltration paths, and unsafe behaviors.
kerrigan_relevance: YARA pattern library is directly importable into Kerrigan's Overmind safety gating.

name: mcp-scanner
description: Scanner for MCP servers covering tools, prompts, resources, package risk, malware indicators, and deployment readiness checks.
use_case: Pre-deployment MCP server security review. Catches tool poisoning, SSRF vectors, and package substitution attacks.
kerrigan_relevance: Relevant when Kerrigan integrates with external MCP tools — scan before connecting.

name: agentic-radar
description: CLI security scanner for agentic workflows (LangGraph, CrewAI, n8n, etc.). Maps tool/data flows and flags security risks in multi-agent pipelines.
use_case: Security review of LangGraph or CrewAI workflow definitions. Visualizes data flow, flags trust boundaries.
kerrigan_relevance: If Kerrigan is extended to multi-agent orchestration, agentic-radar scans the resulting workflow graph.

name: asamm
description: Agentic SAMM — OWASP SAMM extension for AI-driven development. Entry-point-based threat taxonomy with 17 controls across 5 SAMM functions (Governance, Design, Implementation, Verification, Operations) at L1/L2/L3 maturity.
use_case: AI governance and secure-by-design framework for organizations deploying AI coding agents. Maps to NIST AI RMF.
kerrigan_relevance: Direct CyberGuard integration — maps to NIST AI RMF 1.0 governance docs already produced. Use asamm controls as compliance checklist.

name: agent-threat-rules
description: Open versioned machine-readable detection rule format for AI-agent threats: prompt injection, tool poisoning, MCP attacks, skill compromise. Engine-agnostic, converts to Splunk/Elastic/SARIF. Called Sigma for agents.
use_case: Standardized detection rules for AI agent threat categories. Import into SIEM or custom detection pipelines.
kerrigan_relevance: Overmind can import ATR rules as a structured blocklist — augments current hard-block patterns with versioned community rules.

name: AgentDojo
description: Benchmark environment for evaluating prompt-injection attacks and defenses in tool-using LLM agents. From ETH Zurich SPY Lab.
use_case: Benchmarking agent security — test your agent against known prompt injection scenarios and measure defense effectiveness.
kerrigan_relevance: Use to benchmark Kerrigan's Overmind defense against AgentDojo's prompt injection suite before deployment.

name: agentguard
description: Real-time security layer for coding agents. Hooks scan every new skill before execution, block dangerous actions, run daily posture patrols, track which skill triggered each action. Includes Web3-specific security checks.
use_case: Runtime enforcement for AI coding agent deployments. Wraps agent execution with pre-execution skill scanning.
kerrigan_relevance: Complementary to SecureHarnessRunner — agentguard adds pre-execution skill scanning; SecureHarnessRunner adds post-compilation sandboxing.

name: defenseclaw
description: Enforcement and evidence layer for agentic deployments: static CodeGuard checks, sandboxing, registry ingestion with SSRF guards, audit and observability.
use_case: Enterprise-grade agent enforcement with audit trails, sandbox execution, and SSRF protection for external tool calls.
kerrigan_relevance: SecureHarnessRunner + Overmind already cover core sandbox + safety gate. defenseclaw adds enterprise audit trail — relevant for CyberGuard enterprise tier.

name: modelscan
description: Scans ML model files for unsafe serialization patterns and embedded code. Detects model serialization attacks in pickle, PyTorch, TensorFlow, and Keras formats.
use_case: Pre-load scan of any downloaded model checkpoint. Run before loading any .pt, .pkl, or .h5 file.
kerrigan_relevance: Run modelscan on Kerrigan's own checkpoint files and any HuggingFace models pulled during training. Add to data pipeline.

name: fickling
description: Python pickle decompiler, rewriter, and static analyzer for inspecting and detecting malicious pickle and PyTorch payloads. From Trail of Bits.
use_case: Deep inspection of .pkl and .pt files. Decompiles pickle opcodes, detects embedded code execution, rewrites safe versions.
kerrigan_relevance: Pair with modelscan — fickling gives decompiled view of any suspicious checkpoint before Kerrigan loads it.

name: picklescan
description: Lightweight CLI and library for detecting suspicious Python pickle operations in ML and model artifacts. Fast, no heavy dependencies.
use_case: CI/CD gate for model artifact uploads. Lightweight enough to run on every push in GitHub Actions.
kerrigan_relevance: Add to Kerrigan's data pipeline as a pre-load checkpoint gate. One command, zero config.

name: PentestGPT
description: Original USENIX 2024 LLM pentest agent, re-released as an autonomous pipeline. Session management, task decomposition, tool integration, and multi-step exploitation chains.
use_case: Guided or autonomous penetration testing. Decomposes engagement objectives into tasks and executes with LLM reasoning.
kerrigan_relevance: Closest analog to Kerrigan's EvolutionaryLoop at the engagement level — PentestGPT handles recon-to-exploit; Kerrigan handles harness-to-crash.

name: PentAGI
description: Fully autonomous multi-agent pentest framework with Docker sandboxing. Multiple specialized sub-agents coordinate across recon, exploitation, and reporting phases.
use_case: End-to-end autonomous penetration testing in isolated Docker environments. Multi-agent coordination across attack phases.
kerrigan_relevance: Architecture reference — Abathur routing + specialized experts mirrors PentAGI's multi-agent coordination model.

name: CAI
description: Modular bug-bounty-ready agent framework supporting 300+ LLM models. Cybersecurity AI from Alias Robotics. Strong benchmark results on real bug bounty targets.
use_case: Bug bounty automation with model-agnostic support. Drop in any LLM backend, plug into real targets.
kerrigan_relevance: Model-agnostic wrapper pattern relevant to Kerrigan's Ollama fallback — CAI shows how to abstract across LLM backends cleanly.

name: hackingBuddyGPT
description: Minimal (~50 LOC core) research framework for LLM-driven Linux privilege escalation and web pentesting. Published at FSE 2023. Intentionally minimal for research reproducibility.
use_case: Research baseline for LLM-driven priv-esc. Run against CTF or lab Linux targets to benchmark LLM pentest capability.
kerrigan_relevance: Study the 50-LOC core — demonstrates minimum viable LLM pentest loop. Inform Kerrigan's loop/evolution.py simplification.

name: Nebula
description: AI pentesting CLI assistant with local-LLM support (Llama-3.1, Mistral, DeepSeek). Guides human pentesters with AI suggestions while keeping operator in control.
use_case: Human-in-the-loop pentesting assistant. Suggests next steps, interprets tool output, runs on local models.
kerrigan_relevance: Local-LLM pentest assistant pattern — same as Kerrigan's Ollama fallback mode. Nebula's command routing is worth studying.

name: HexStrike-AI
description: MCP server exposing 150+ security tools (nmap, gobuster, nuclei, sqlmap, etc.) to AI agents. Lets any MCP-compatible agent call real security tools by name.
use_case: Give any AI agent access to the full security tool stack via MCP. Wraps nmap, gobuster, nuclei, sqlmap, and 146 more.
kerrigan_relevance: High priority integration — connect HexStrike-AI as an MCP source into Kerrigan's evolve loop for post-crash tool chaining.

name: PentestAgent
description: Black-box AI pentest framework with MCP integration, multi-agent spawning, and persistent sessions across engagements.
use_case: Black-box engagement automation with session persistence. Spawns specialized sub-agents per attack phase.
kerrigan_relevance: MCP integration pattern — how PentestAgent connects to tools via MCP informs Kerrigan's HexStrike integration.

name: Pentest-Swarm-AI
description: Swarm-intelligence multi-agent pentest using stigmergic blackboard coordination written in Go. Agents communicate through shared state rather than direct messaging.
use_case: Highly parallel pentest with emergent coordination. Agents deposit findings on a shared blackboard; others pick up and continue.
kerrigan_relevance: Blackboard coordination pattern is architecturally relevant to Kerrigan's Creep memory — both are shared persistent state for agent coordination.

name: Vulnhuntr
description: Zero-shot vulnerability discovery in Python repos via LLM call-chain analysis. Credited with discovering a 0-day RCE in Ragflow. Traces data flow from entry points through the full call chain to sinks.
use_case: Python codebase vulnerability discovery. Point at a repo, get CVE-quality findings with call-chain evidence.
kerrigan_relevance: Python call-chain analysis complements Kerrigan's C/C++ focus — use Vulnhuntr on Python wrappers around C targets.

name: IRIS
description: Neurosymbolic SAST combining LLMs with CodeQL for Java vulnerability detection. Merges LLM semantic understanding with formal CodeQL taint analysis.
use_case: Java application security scanning with hybrid LLM + CodeQL analysis. Higher precision than either approach alone.
kerrigan_relevance: Neurosymbolic approach (LLM + formal analysis) mirrors Kerrigan's planned hybrid static-dynamic analysis. Study IRIS architecture.

name: xvulnhuntr
description: Fork of Vulnhuntr extending support to C#, Java, and Go in addition to Python. From Compass Security. Archived but functional.
use_case: Multi-language vulnerability discovery beyond Python. Same call-chain LLM analysis applied to C#, Java, Go.
kerrigan_relevance: Language coverage expansion — Go and C# targets that Kerrigan's C/C++ harnesses can't directly fuzz.

name: claude-code-security-review
description: Official Claude-based semantic SAST GitHub Action that reviews PR diffs for security issues. Anthropic-maintained.
use_case: Automated PR security review in GitHub Actions. Every PR gets a Claude-powered security analysis.
kerrigan_relevance: CI integration for Kerrigan's own codebase — auto-review kerrigan-fantasma PRs with this action.

name: oss-fuzz-gen
description: LLM-driven fuzz harness generation for OSS-Fuzz. Reported 26 real vulnerabilities including CVE-2024-9143 in OpenSSL. Google-maintained, continuously running.
use_case: Automated fuzz harness generation for open-source C/C++ libraries. Integrates with OSS-Fuzz infrastructure.
kerrigan_relevance: Closest existing system to Kerrigan's ClosedLoopCompiler + MutationFuzzer. Study oss-fuzz-gen's harness generation prompts directly.

name: PromptFuzz
description: LLM-mutated prompts to generate fuzz drivers for C/C++ libraries written in Rust. Mutates prompts iteratively to improve harness coverage.
use_case: Coverage-guided fuzz driver generation for C/C++ with Rust harnesses. Prompt mutation loop improves harness quality.
kerrigan_relevance: Prompt mutation for harness improvement is exactly what Kerrigan's EvolutionaryLoop does — compare approaches.

name: Fuzz4All
description: Universal LLM-based fuzzer across compilers and languages. ICSE 2024 paper. Handles C, C++, Python, Java, Go, Rust, JavaScript — same framework, different targets.
use_case: Language-agnostic fuzzing. Adapts to target language automatically, generates semantically valid inputs.
kerrigan_relevance: Universal fuzzer architecture is a roadmap for Kerrigan beyond C/C++ — Fuzz4All shows how to generalize the MutationFuzzer.

name: ChatAFL
description: LLM-guided protocol fuzzing extending AFLNet. NDSS 2024. Uses LLM to generate protocol-aware mutations that respect message structure.
use_case: Protocol fuzzing where pure mutation breaks message structure. LLM maintains protocol semantics during mutation.
kerrigan_relevance: Protocol fuzzing is a gap in Kerrigan's current MutationFuzzer — ChatAFL's semantic mutation approach fills it directly.

name: TitanFuzz
description: First LLM-based fuzzer targeting PyTorch and TensorFlow. ISSTA 2023. Generates API-sequence tests that expose ML framework bugs.
use_case: Fuzzing ML frameworks themselves — finds bugs in PyTorch and TensorFlow APIs.
kerrigan_relevance: Relevant to fuzzing Kerrigan's own training dependencies — TitanFuzz can target PyTorch bugs in the training pipeline.

name: LLMFuzzer
description: First open-source fuzzing framework for LLM API integrations. Tests LLM-powered applications for prompt injection, jailbreaks, and unexpected behavior at API boundaries.
use_case: Fuzz-test your LLM API integration. Find prompt injection vectors, unexpected refusals, and data leakage at LLM API calls.
kerrigan_relevance: Use LLMFuzzer to test Kerrigan's own Ollama API integration and Overmind safety gate for bypasses.

name: ps-fuzz
description: System-prompt hardening fuzzer. 16 attack types across 16 LLM providers. Identifies system prompt leakage and injection vulnerabilities.
use_case: Harden your LLM system prompt against injection. Run 16 attack types, get a hardening report.
kerrigan_relevance: Run against Kerrigan's config/Modelfile system prompt and CyberGuard's lite model system prompt — identify injection vectors before deployment.

name: FuzzyAI
description: Automated LLM fuzzer for jailbreaks and prompt injection from CyberArk. Tests guardrails and content policies at scale.
use_case: Enterprise-scale LLM guardrail testing. Automated jailbreak discovery across custom and commercial LLM deployments.
kerrigan_relevance: Use FuzzyAI to red-team Kerrigan's Overmind safety gate — find jailbreaks before adversaries do.

name: ai-prompt-fuzzer
description: Burp Suite extension for fuzzing GenAI and LLM prompts. Integrates directly into Burp workflow for testing LLM-powered web applications.
use_case: Web app pentest with LLM components. Fuzz LLM API endpoints from within Burp Suite during web application testing.
kerrigan_relevance: If CyberGuard exposes LLM functionality via a web interface, use ai-prompt-fuzzer to test it.

name: trs
description: LLM plus ChromaDB tool to summarize threat reports and extract MITRE TTPs and IOCs from unstructured text. Outputs structured intelligence.
use_case: Threat report digestion. Feed raw PDF or text threat reports, get structured TTPs and IOCs for SIEM ingestion.
kerrigan_relevance: ChromaDB TTP extraction mirrors Kerrigan's Creep memory architecture — same vector store, complementary use case. Consider merging data schemas.

name: TI-Mindmap-GPT
description: Streamlit application for AI-powered threat intelligence. Generates summaries, mindmaps, IOC and TTP extraction, and ATT&CK Navigator layers from threat reports.
use_case: Analyst-facing threat intelligence visualization. Upload report, get mindmap and Navigator layer for briefings.
kerrigan_relevance: CyberGuard UI extension — TI-Mindmap-GPT's Streamlit approach shows how to visualize Kerrigan's Creep memory findings.

name: aiocrioc
description: LLM plus OCR IOC extraction tool. Pulls indicators of compromise from images, screenshots, and PDFs where text extraction fails.
use_case: Extract IOCs from screenshots of reports, images of threat feeds, or scanned PDFs. OCR + LLM pipeline.
kerrigan_relevance: Feeds IOCs into Kerrigan's Creep memory from non-text sources — complements trs which handles text-only input.

name: IATelligence
description: Explains imported Windows APIs in PE files via GPT and maps to MITRE ATT&CK. Static PE analysis with AI-powered TTP mapping.
use_case: Malware triage via import table analysis. Feed a PE binary, get MITRE ATT&CK technique mappings from its imports.
kerrigan_relevance: Windows PE analysis is outside Kerrigan's current Linux/kernel focus — IATelligence extends coverage to Windows malware targets.

name: MCP_Security
description: MCP server for querying the ORKL threat intelligence API. Exposes threat intelligence data to any MCP-compatible agent.
use_case: Real-time threat intelligence lookup from MCP-compatible agents. Query actor profiles, campaign data, and IOCs via ORKL.
kerrigan_relevance: High priority — connect MCP_Security as a Kerrigan tool source. Abathur routes threat-intel queries here automatically.

name: AI-SOC-Agent
description: Black Hat 2025 MCP server exposing security investigation tools (ELK, IRIS DFIR) to AI agents. Demonstrated at Black Hat 2025.
use_case: AI-assisted SOC investigation. Agent queries ELK logs, creates IRIS cases, and correlates findings automatically.
kerrigan_relevance: CyberGuard integration — AI-SOC-Agent's ELK integration complements CyberGuard's GeoIP analytics and incident reporting.

name: agentic-soc-platform
description: Full agentic SOC platform using LangGraph and Dify with local LLM support. End-to-end alert-to-report automation.
use_case: Build a complete agentic SOC workflow. LangGraph orchestrates alert ingestion, triage, investigation, and report generation.
kerrigan_relevance: CyberGuard roadmap — shows how to build the full agentic SOC pipeline that CyberGuard's lite model would power.

name: AttackGen
description: LLM-driven incident response scenario generator using MITRE ATT&CK and ATLAS frameworks. Creates realistic tabletop exercise scenarios.
use_case: Tabletop exercise generation. Feed your org profile, get a realistic IR scenario mapped to MITRE ATT&CK techniques.
kerrigan_relevance: CyberGuard feature — generate IR scenarios mapped to findings from Kerrigan's evolutionary loop.

name: GCPAX
description: LLM-assisted GhidraScript for automated binary analysis. Uses LLM to interpret Ghidra decompiler output and generate analysis reports.
use_case: Automated binary analysis with Ghidra. LLM interprets decompiled functions, identifies patterns, generates analyst notes.
kerrigan_relevance: Extends Kerrigan's analysis surface to compiled binaries — pair with evolutionary loop for harness-to-binary analysis pipeline.

name: PyRIT
description: Python Risk Identification Toolkit for LLM red-teaming from Microsoft Azure. Automated multi-turn adversarial testing of LLM systems.
use_case: Enterprise LLM red-teaming. Automated adversarial probing of LLM applications for safety, security, and policy violations.
kerrigan_relevance: Red-team Kerrigan's own LLM outputs with PyRIT — verify Overmind catches what PyRIT finds.

name: garak
description: LLM vulnerability scanner — the nmap for LLMs. Tests for prompt injection, jailbreaks, data leakage, hallucination, and 50+ other probe types.
use_case: Comprehensive LLM vulnerability assessment. Run all 50+ probe types, get a structured vulnerability report.
kerrigan_relevance: Run garak against Kerrigan's inference endpoint and CyberGuard's lite model endpoint — full vulnerability baseline before deployment.

name: LLM Honeypot
description: LLM-powered honeypot that generates convincing fake responses to attackers probing AI systems. Detects adversarial probing and logs attacker behavior.
use_case: Deploy a honeypot LLM endpoint that detects and logs adversarial probing attempts.
kerrigan_relevance: CyberGuard deception layer — deploy alongside real endpoints to detect attackers probing the AI system.

name: NYU-CTF-Bench
description: Benchmark of 200 CTF challenges for evaluating LLM exploit-solving capability. Covers pwn, crypto, web, forensics, and reverse engineering categories.
use_case: Benchmark Kerrigan's exploit capability against standardized CTF challenges.
kerrigan_relevance: Primary benchmark for Kerrigan's exploit capability — run NYU-CTF-Bench to measure KerriganCore against baseline LLMs.

name: Cybench
description: Benchmark for evaluating LLM cybersecurity task performance across 40 CTF challenges from 4 competitions. Tracks agent scaffolding and model capability separately.
use_case: Model-agnostic cybersecurity benchmark. Separate agent scaffolding from model capability in your evaluation.
kerrigan_relevance: Cybench isolates model capability from scaffolding — use to measure KerriganCore alone vs KerriganCore + Abathur routing.

name: CloudGPT
description: LLM-powered CloudFormation and IaC security review. Scans CloudFormation, Terraform, and ARM templates for security misconfigurations.
use_case: IaC security review with LLM explanations. Get human-readable explanations of CloudFormation misconfigurations.
kerrigan_relevance: CyberGuard cloud module — extends NIST compliance mapping to IaC templates. Integrates with existing NIST 800-53 mapping.
